question: What is the main goal of Family Life Education in the community?

options.A: Promoting overall well-being and disease prevention
options.B: Treating acute medical and surgical emergencies
options.D: Diagnosing rare genetic disorders in infants

explanation: Family Life Education is all about helping people stay healthy and preventing problems before they start, rather than treating emergencies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h1)

question: Why is Family Life Education an important part of primary health care?

options.A: It eliminates all infectious diseases from the community
options.B: It guarantees financial stability for every household
options.C: It completely replaces the need for hospital-based doctors
options.D: It equips individuals with knowledge to make healthy life choices

explanation: When people get the right information about their bodies and relationships, they can make smart choices to protect their health! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h1)

question: What is the core aim of Family Life Education?

options.B: Enforcing strict legal penalties for domestic disputes
options.D: Building strong, healthy families and communities

explanation: FLE focuses on giving people the skills and knowledge they need to build happy, healthy homes and communities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h2)

question: Why do nurses focus on empowerment in Family Life Education?

options.A: It forces community members to adopt identical lifestyles
options.B: It ensures that nurses make all final decisions for clients
options.C: It helps learners build critical thinking for better choices
options.D: It prevents individuals from questioning health policies

explanation: Empowerment means giving people the tools to think for themselves so they can make the best health decisions for their own lives. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h2)

question: In the female reproductive system, where does fertilization usually take place?
explanation: The fallopian tube is where the magic happens! It is the pathway where a sperm meets and fertilizes the egg. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h3)

question: What is the main job of the testes in the male body?
explanation: The testes are the male reproductive glands responsible for making sperm and the hormone testosterone. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h3)

question: What triggers the physical changes of puberty?

options.A: Hormonal surges from the endocrine system
options.C: Rapid expansion of skeletal muscle mass

explanation: Puberty kicks off when the brain sends signals to the endocrine system to release hormones that drive body changes. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h4)

question: A teenager is worried about sudden mood swings and body changes. As a nurse, what should you say?

options.A: Explain that these emotional and physical shifts are a normal part of adolescent development
options.B: Refer the teenager immediately to a psychiatric hospital for evaluation
options.C: Tell the client to ignore the feelings because they do not matter
options.D: Prescribe heavy sedative medications to stabilize the mood

explanation: A little reassurance goes a long way! Letting teens know their changes are normal helps calm their worries. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h4)

question: Which type of sexually transmitted infection can usually be cured with antibiotics?
explanation: Bacterial STIs, like gonorrhea and chlamydia, can be knocked out easily with the right course of antibiotics. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h5)

question: Why do health workers always promote barrier methods like condoms?

options.A: They replace the need for routine clinic check-ups entirely
options.B: They provide dual protection against both STIs and unintended pregnancy
options.C: They act as permanent hormonal regulators for the body
options.D: They guarantee complete immunity against every known human virus

explanation: Condoms are great because they block germs and sperm at the same time, protecting against both infections and pregnancy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h5)

question: Which of these is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC)?
explanation: An Intrauterine Device (IUD) is placed in the womb and provides protection for years, but can be removed anytime you want. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h6)

question: Why is good contraceptive counseling so important in community health?

options.A: It guarantees that couples will never experience any side effects
options.B: It eliminates the need for any further nursing interaction
options.C: It forces every citizen to use hormonal birth control methods
options.D: It helps clients choose a method that fits their health needs and lifestyle

explanation: Everyone's body and life is different. Counseling helps clients pick the birth control method that works best for them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of values clarification exercises?

options.A: Helping individuals examine their personal beliefs and priorities
options.B: Imposing the nurse's personal moral standards on the client
options.C: Testing the client on medical terminology and anatomy

explanation: Values clarification helps people figure out what truly matters to them so they can make confident life decisions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h7)

question: How do good communication skills help families stay healthy?

options.A: They dictate strict financial rules for family members
options.B: They reduce conflict and help members express needs clearly
options.C: They ensure that arguments never happen in any household
options.D: They replace the need for physical health checkups

explanation: When family members talk openly and listen well, they solve problems faster and keep peace in the home. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a nurse's role in community Family Life Education?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations in schools
options.B: Acting as an advocate for adolescent health
options.C: Serving as an educator for health promotion

explanation: Nurses do not do surgeries in schools! Our focus is on health education, counseling, and supporting our clients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h8)

question: Why should nurses involve local community leaders when starting health programs?

options.A: It gives leaders legal authority to write nursing prescriptions
options.B: It replaces the need for trained healthcare professionals
options.C: It builds local support and ensures programs respect cultural values
options.D: It prevents community members from asking questions

explanation: Working with local leaders builds trust and makes sure the community welcomes and accepts the health program. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h8)
